summary: 脑中反复响起一段旋律的现象称为“耳虫”，常在注意力负担较低时出现。研究比较了近期接触、跟唱、心情和旋律结构的作用，尚难用单一因素预测哪首歌会挥之不去。
logic: 测量脑中音乐与原曲的相似度

paragraphs.brief: 脑内循环旋律如何研究
sentences: Ever had a song stuck in your head, playing on an endless loop?
你是否有过一首歌在脑子里不停循环的经历？
Scientists call them ‘involuntary musical images’, or ‘earworms’, and a wave of new research is shining light on why they occur and what can be learned from them.
科学家称这类体验为“不自主音乐意象”，俗称“耳虫”。新一波研究正在解释它为何发生，以及它能告诉我们什么。
Some neuroscientists and cognitive psychologists are studying earworms to explore the mysteries of memory and the part of the brain that is beyond our conscious control.
一些神经科学家和认知心理学家研究“耳虫”，希望借此探索记忆的奥秘，并了解大脑中不受意识支配的活动。

‘The idea that we have full control over our thought processes is an illusion,’ says psychologist Lauren Stewart, who founded the master’s program in music, mind and brain at Goldsmiths, University of London, UK, where recent research has taken place.
伦敦大学金史密斯学院开设音乐、心智与大脑硕士项目的心理学家劳伦·斯图尔特说：“以为我们能完全掌控思维过程，是一种错觉。”近期研究就在该院进行。
Researchers haven’t been able to watch what happens in the brain when earworms occur, because they happen unpredictably.
由于耳虫的出现不可预测，研究者还没能直接观察到它发生时大脑里有什么变化。
Much of what is known about them comes from surveys, questionnaires, diaries and lab experiments.
目前关于耳虫的大部分认识来自调查、问卷、日记和实验室研究。
paragraphs.gist: 难以自控、反复在脑中播放的“耳虫”是研究记忆的一扇窗，但它出现得不可预测，使研究者主要依靠日记、问卷与实验。

paragraphs.brief: 节拍准确度与相关脑区
sentences: A Goldsmiths study published in the journal Memory and Cognition this year showed that the singing we hear in our heads tends to be true to actual recordings.
金史密斯学院今年发表于《记忆与认知》的一项研究发现，我们脑中响起的歌声往往相当忠实于原版录音。
Researchers had 17 volunteers tap to the beat of any earworm they heard during a four-day period while a device attached to their wrist recorded their movements.
研究者请十七位志愿者在四天内每当脑中出现耳虫，就随它敲打节拍，由手腕上的装置记录动作。
The tapping tempos were within 10% of the tempos of the original recordings.
所敲节奏与原版录音的速度相差不超过百分之十。

Another Goldsmiths study, published this year in Consciousness and Cognition, found that people who report hearing earworms often, and find them most intrusive, have slightly different brain structures, with more gray matter in areas associated with processing emotions.
该院今年发表于《意识与认知》的另一项研究发现，常出现耳虫、也觉得它最扰人的受访者脑结构略有不同，在加工情绪的脑区有更多灰质。
paragraphs.gist: 四天的手腕记录显示，人们敲出的脑内旋律节拍与原曲相差不超过一成，另一研究还发现常受耳虫困扰者的情绪加工区灰质更多。

paragraphs.brief: 闲下来更容易出现耳虫
sentences: Studies also show that the music in our heads often starts playing during times of ‘low cognitive load’, such as while showering, getting dressed, walking, or doing chores.
研究还发现，旋律通常在认知负担较低时开始在脑中播放，例如洗澡、穿衣、散步或做家务时。
Dr Stewart likens earworms to ‘sonic screen savers’ that keep the mind entertained while it is otherwise unoccupied.
斯图尔特把耳虫比作“有声音的屏保程序”，当心思没有别的事要忙时，它就给大脑找点乐子。
She and her colleagues tested that theory by having volunteers listen to songs and giving them various tasks afterwards.
她和她的同事测试了这一理论，让志愿者听歌，然后给他们各种任务。
The volunteers who sat idly for the next five minutes were the most likely to report hearing the music in their heads.
接下来五分钟坐着无事可做的志愿者，最常报告听到了脑中的音乐。
Dr Stewart observed that the more challenging the activity, the less likely the volunteers were to hear the music.
斯图尔特观察到，任务越有挑战，志愿者越不容易听到脑内音乐。
Diary studies also show songs tend to match people’s moods and therefore they are not random.
日记研究还显示，歌曲往往与人们的情绪相匹配，因此不是随机的。
If you are energized and upbeat, an earworm that occurs is likely to be uptempo too.
人若精力充沛、心情振奋，出现的耳虫往往也是快节奏的。
paragraphs.gist: 闲坐比专注做难题更容易让旋律钻进脑海，日记也发现歌曲节奏往往与当时情绪相配，耳虫因此并非完全随机。

paragraphs.brief: 近期听过的背景音乐最易重现
sentences: Songs the brain fixates on are usually those it has been exposed to recently, surveys show, which is why tunes getting heavy radio play frequently top the earworm charts.
调查发现，大脑反复播放的通常是最近听过的歌，所以电台频繁播出的曲调常在耳虫排行榜上居前。
Even tunes you may have heard but didn’t pay attention to can worm their way into your subconscious, says Ira Hyman, a psychologist at Western Washington University in Bellingham, USA.
美国西华盛顿大学心理学家艾拉·海曼说，即使是听过却没留意的曲子，也可能悄悄进入潜意识。

In an unpublished study there, participants who listened to music while doing other tasks were more likely to report that the songs returned as earworms later on, compared with participants who simply listened.
该校一项尚未发表的研究发现，边做其他事边听音乐的参与者，比专心听歌者更常报告这些歌后来又作为耳虫出现。
paragraphs.gist: 近期频繁播放的曲子最易形成耳虫，一项初步实验甚至发现，边做事边听歌的人比专心听的人更容易在后来反复想起旋律。

paragraphs.brief: 歌曲残片与未完成效应
sentences: Some earworms are just fragments of a song that repeat like a broken record.
有些耳虫只是一首歌的片段，像唱片卡针一样反复播放。
So, when the mind hits a part of a song it can’t remember, it loops back rather than moving on.
一碰到记不起的部分，脑中的乐曲就会从头绕回来，没法继续往下。
That could make an earworm even more entrenched, Dr Hyman says.
海曼说，这种循环可能让旋律更难甩掉。

According to a theory known as the Zeigarnik effect, named for a Soviet psychologist, Bluma Zeigarnik, unfinished thoughts and activities weigh on the mind more heavily than those that are completed, although experiments exposing students to interrupted songs have yielded mixed results.
以苏联心理学家布卢玛·蔡加尼克命名的“蔡加尼克效应”认为，未完成的念头与事情比已完成的更让人挂心，但给学生播放中途打断的歌曲并未得到一致结果。
paragraphs.gist: 想不起歌曲的下一段时，大脑可能返回熟悉片段不断重播，这与未完成之事更挂心的理论相符，但打断歌曲的实验结果并不一致。

paragraphs.brief: 想象和听觉共享神经网络
sentences: Researchers say they can’t pinpoint a spot in the brain where earworms live.
研究者说，无法锁定大脑中一个专门产生耳虫的部位。

Imaging studies by Andrea Halpern at Bucknell University, in Lewisburg, USA, have shown that deliberately imagining music and actually listening to music activate many of the same neurological networks.
美国巴克内尔大学安德里娅·哈尔彭的脑成像研究表明，有意想象音乐和实际听音乐会激活许多相同的神经网络。

Dr Halpern’s earlier studies showed that when subjects listened to the first few notes of familiar music, areas in the right frontal and superior temporal portions of the brain became activated, along with the supplementary motor area at the top, which is typically involved in remembering sequences.
她早期的研究显示，受试者听到熟悉旋律最初几个音符时，右侧额叶和上颞部，以及通常参与记忆顺序的脑顶辅助运动区会被激活。
When the same subjects listened to unfamiliar music and were asked to recall it, there was activity in the left frontal portions of the brain instead.
相同的受试者听到陌生音乐并尝试回忆时，活动却出现在大脑左侧额叶。
paragraphs.gist: 主动想象音乐和实际听音乐会激活许多共同网络，而回忆熟曲与新曲时活动的脑区不同，目前还不能把耳虫定位到单一部位。

paragraphs.brief: 重复旋律与不规则音程
sentences: One factor that makes some songs stick might be repetition.
重复可能是某些歌曲挥之不去的一个原因。

‘Repetition leads to familiarity which leads to anticipation, which is satisfied by hearing the song,’ says John Seabrook, author of The Song Machine: Inside the Hit Factory, about how producers pump pop songs full of aural ‘hooks’, the punchy melodic phrases designed to target the brain and leave it wanting more.
《歌曲机器：热门歌曲工厂内幕》的作者约翰·西布鲁克说：“重复让人熟悉，熟悉带来期待，再次听到歌曲就满足了那份期待。”制作人因此在流行歌曲中加入许多“钩子”，也就是让人想再听的短促抓耳旋律。
The researchers are comparing the melodic structure of 100 often mentioned songs with 100 similarly popular songs that weren’t cited as earworms, to assess the difference.
研究者将一百首常被报告为耳虫的歌曲与一百首同样流行、却未被提及的歌曲作旋律结构比较。
Songs with earworm potential appear to share certain features: a repeating pattern of ups and downs in pitch, and irregular musical intervals.
容易成为耳虫的歌似乎有某些共同特点，例如音高起伏模式反复出现，音程却不规则。
paragraphs.gist: 反复听到的旋律会产生期待，对照常成耳虫和同样流行的其他曲目后，研究者注意到重复的音高起伏与不规则音程可能尤其抓耳。

paragraphs.brief: 铃声实验与年龄差异待检验
sentences: The researchers plan next to test their results in reverse, and play ringtones from songs of both the earworm and non-earworm variety for volunteers several times a day to see which ones get stuck.
研究人员计划反过来检验结论，每天数次向志愿者播放两类歌曲的铃声，看看哪些旋律真的会黏在脑中。
Drs Stewart and Halpern are now working together to recruit survey participants for a study looking at whether people at different stages of life experience earworms differently.
斯图尔特和哈尔潘目前正合作招募受试者，考察处于不同人生阶段的人经历“耳虫”现象时有何差别。
‘You can argue that older people might get them more often because they know more songs,’ Dr Halpern says.
哈尔彭说：“老年人熟悉的歌更多，按说也许会更常出现耳虫。
‘But the few responses we have so far indicate that they have earworms less often.
但迄今收到的少量答复显示，他们出现耳虫的频率反而较低。
It could be that they don’t play music as often as younger people do.’
也许是因为他们不像年轻人那样经常播放音乐。”
paragraphs.gist: 研究者拟反过来用手机铃声检验旋律是否容易黏住人，也在比较年龄差异，少量初步答复显示老年人报告的耳虫反而较少。

items.en: a description of the characteristics common to songs with earworms
items.zh: 容易在人脑中反复回响的歌曲有哪些共同特征。
items.why: 容易形成“耳虫”的歌曲常有重复的音高起伏和不规则音程，G段给出了共有的旋律特征。

items.en: a justification for research into earworms
items.zh: 研究“耳虫”现象，也就是旋律反复在脑海中响起，有什么理由。
items.why: 研究耳虫能帮助了解记忆及人无法有意识控制的大脑活动，解释了科学家为什么研究它。

items.en: a description of the brain’s reaction to known and unknown songs
items.zh: 描述大脑对熟悉和陌生的歌曲分别有什么反应。
items.why: 听到熟悉曲调时右额叶等区域被激活，回忆陌生曲调时则是左额叶活动，两种反应在F段对照。

items.en: details of proposed research into the frequency with which earworms occur in different age groups.
items.zh: 一项拟议研究的细节，该研究将比较不同年龄群体出现“耳虫”现象的频率。
items.why: 研究者计划招募处于不同人生阶段的人，比较各年龄组耳虫出现的频率。

items.en: They proved this by asking volunteers to record the rhythm of music using a monitor on their ________.
items.zh: 为验证这一点，研究者让志愿者用戴在________上的监测器记录音乐节奏。
items.why: 志愿者随脑中的音乐敲打节拍，由戴在手腕上的装置记录动作。因此所问的佩戴部位是 wrist。

items.en: Further research has demonstrated that those who hear earworms more frequently have brains that may deal with ________ differently from other people, Dr Stewart also believes that the brain is ____ (Q20) by earworms when it is not focused on a task.
items.zh: 后续研究发现，脑中经常反复响起旋律的人，处理________的方式可能与他人不同。斯图尔特博士还认为，大脑没有专注于某项任务时，这些旋律可以让它________（Q20）。
items.why: 更常出现“耳虫”的人，大脑处理 emotions（情绪）的方式可能与其他人不同。

items.en: Further research has demonstrated that those who hear earworms more frequently have brains that may deal with ____ (Q19) differently from other people, Dr Stewart also believes that the brain is ________ by earworms when it is not focused on a task.
items.zh: 后续研究发现，脑中经常反复响起旋律的人，处理________（Q19）的方式可能与他人不同。斯图尔特博士还认为，大脑没有专注于某项任务时，这些旋律可以让它________。
items.why: 如果大脑没有被任务占用，反复响起的旋律就能给它提供消遣，原文用 entertained 表达这一点。

items.en: In Fact, a reduction in the occurrence of earworms was found to be directly related to how ________ the task was.
items.zh: 研究发现，这类旋律在脑中出现的次数减少，与所做任务有多________直接相关。
items.why: 定位句说：“斯图尔特观察到，任务越有挑战，志愿者越不容易听到脑内音乐。”

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Some musicians create music that is intentionally memorable.
items.zh: 有些音乐人会刻意创作让人过耳难忘的音乐。

items.en: People are unable to completely regulate how they think
items.zh: 人无法完全控制自己的思维活动。

items.en: We can remember songs without knowing that we have heard them.
items.zh: 即使没有意识到自己曾听过某首歌，我们也可能记得它。

items.en: Thinking about music has a similar effect on the brain to hearing music.
items.zh: 在脑中想象音乐与实际听音乐，对大脑产生的影响相似。

items.en: Earworms are more persistent when only a short section of the song is constantly replayed.
items.zh: 如果脑海里一再重复的只是一首歌中的一小段，这种旋律萦绕不去的现象就会持续更久。

pairs: 题干用形容词，定位句改用同词根的副词。
points: 研究耳虫能帮助了解记忆及人无法有意识控制的大脑活动，解释了科学家为什么研究它。
定位句说：“斯图尔特观察到，任务越有挑战，志愿者越不容易听到脑内音乐。”
clauses: ‘ …,’ says psychologist Lauren Stewart, who founded the master’s program in music, mind and brain at Goldsmiths, University of London, UK, where recent research has taken place.
“The idea that we have full control over our thought processes is an illusion”补足 says 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 says 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Researchers had 17 volunteers tap to the beat of any earworm they heard during a four-day period ….
连接词 while 引出“while a device attached to their wrist recorded their movements”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Scientists investigate ‘earworms’, the music we can’t get out of our heads
科学家研究的是「耳虫」现象，也就是某段旋律在脑海里反复播放，怎么也甩不掉。
vocabulary: 在脑中反复回响的曲调
